branchName.instructions:
Use <type>/<scope>/<short-description> in lowercase kebab-case.

Types: feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore, perf, build, ci.

Examples:
feat/auth/add-passkey-login
fix/api/handle-empty-response
refactor/search/simplify-ranking
docs/setup/add-local-dev-guide

Include an issue ID when one exists:
fix/ISSUE-123/api-timeout

Keep names descriptive and implementation-neutral. Avoid personal initials, dates, generic names like update/fix/stuff, and generated IDs unless required.

commitMessage.instructions:
Use Conventional Commits:

<type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>

Examples:
feat(auth): add passkey login
fix(api): handle empty provider response
refactor(search): simplify ranking pipeline
test(auth): cover expired session handling

Use the same types as branch names.

Keep each commit focused on one logical change. Write the subject in imperative present tense and explain WHY in the body when the reason is not obvious.

Reference related issues in the footer when applicable.
Use BREAKING CHANGE: for incompatible changes.

Do not use vague messages such as "update code", "fix stuff", "changes", or "WIP".

pullRequest.instructions:
Use this structure:

## Summary
Explain what changed and why in 1-3 concise paragraphs or bullets.

## Changes
List the important implementation changes.

## Test plan
List exactly how the change was verified, including automated tests and relevant manual checks.

## Risks
Describe known risks, edge cases, migrations, compatibility concerns, or write "None".

## Implementation notes
Document non-obvious decisions, constraints, invariants, or follow-up work that future humans or agents should know.

## Related
Link issues, tasks, specs, or dependent PRs when applicable.

Keep the PR focused on one logical change. Mention unrelated changes explicitly rather than hiding them. Include screenshots or recordings for user-visible UI changes.
